newsitem.title: USA: Cuban baseball defectors head for U.S.
newsitem.headline: Cuban baseball defectors head for U.S.

text.p: Three Cuban baseball players were heading for the United States on Wednesday after defecting during a tournament in Chiapas, Mexico, a spokesman for Miami sports promoter Jose Cubas said.
The three players, who fled their Cuban team during the night, were named as Roberto Colina, William Ortega and Jesus Ametller.
"Mr. Cubas is going with the three now towards the U.S. border after they decided to abandon the tournament a little after midnight," spokesman Rene Guim told Reuters.
Colina, 25, Ortega, 21, and Ametller, 22, all played for the club Industriales de La Habana, which was representing Cuba in a tournament of champions in Chiapas.
Guim said the tournament included teams from Mexico, the Dominican Republic and other Latin American countries.
He had no details on how Cubas managed to make contact with the players or arrange the defection.
"He will get in touch with me again when they have reached the (U.S.-Mexican) border to give me details," he said.
He could not say where they would cross.
Cubas is president of the Premier Sports Council, a firm which represents athletes in the United States. It has been the conduit for a number of defections by Cuban baseball players.

Last month the Cuban government suspended for life three members of the national team, German Mesa, Orlando "El Duke" Hernandez and Jorge Luis Toca, who it accused of trying to make contacts with Cubans in Venezuela with the aim of leaving the communist-ruled island.
Although Cubas admits having links with an agent the Cuban authorities have accused of encouraging baseball players to defect, he denies initiating any moves himself.
